blind_solve.my_reasoning: Exertional pressure-type discomfort with regional lateral ST depression and T-wave inversion that deepens on serial tracing plus a rising high-sensitivity troponin is acute myocardial injury in an ischaemic context without ST elevation, i.e. NSTE-ACS.

Inferior STEMI with V4R ST elevation, hypotension, raised JVP and clear lungs is right-ventricular infarction, which is preload dependent, so a cautious fluid challenge with reassessment is the next step and nitrates, diuretics and beta blockade are all contraindicated here.

Diagnostic anterior STEMI at a non-PCI centre with an expected first-medical-contact-to-device time of about four hours (far beyond 120 minutes) and no contraindication calls for fibrinolysis now followed by routine rapid transfer as a pharmacoinvasive strategy, not rescue-only or deferred angiography.

A troponin rise-and-fall compatible with infarction plus dynamic T-wave change is a high-risk NSTE-ACS criterion that resolution of symptoms and normalisation of the tracing do not withdraw, so she needs admission and an early inpatient invasive strategy.
A first wheezing episode at 7 months after a two-to-three day coryzal prodrome with diffuse symmetric wheeze and crackles, equal air entry and mild hypoxaemia is acute viral bronchiolitis.

An improving, feeding, term infant weaned off oxygen on day four of bronchiolitis is lower risk, so repeated structured clinical assessment with intermittent saturation checks is what is indicated; continuous monitoring risks prolonging stay and no diagnostic test is indicated.

Saturation of 88% in room air on two measurements is below the 90% threshold at which oxygen is given, and with stable work of breathing the least support that corrects the deficit is low-flow nasal-prong oxygen rather than high-flow, epinephrine or fluids.

findings: COMPETITOR_WITHOUT_STEM_ANCHOR (option B, Pulmonary embolism): the stem contains no positive feature that would draw a candidate toward PE and instead negates every one. It states 'respiratory rate is 16 breaths/min and oxygen saturation is 97% on room air', 'his chest is clear, his calves are soft and he has had no recent immobility, surgery or travel', and the discomfort 'does not change with posture or deep inspiration'. Against the item's own admitted claim CLM-PE-DIAGNOSIS-01 ('Sudden dyspnea, pleuritic chest pain, hemoptysis, hypoxemia, and venous-thromboembolism risk factors raise plausibility'), the pretest probability written into this stem is essentially zero. Nothing invites the option.

COMPETITOR_WITHOUT_STEM_ANCHOR (option A, Acute aortic dissection): the stem writes out both discriminating features as absent - 'Blood pressure is 148/86 mmHg and equal in both arms' and 'There is no back pain and no pulse deficit' - and additionally negates the onset pattern ('began while he was climbing stairs and has eased only slightly with rest', i.e. explicitly not abrupt and maximal at onset). No stem element pulls toward dissection.

COMPETITOR_WITHOUT_STEM_ANCHOR (option C, Acute pericarditis): 'The discomfort is not sharp, does not change with posture or deep inspiration' negates the character, and the ECG description ('horizontal ST depression with T-wave inversion across the lateral precordial leads') is the opposite of the pattern in claim CLM-PERICARDITIS-01. The distractor rationale itself concedes this: 'which is the opposite pattern'. An option whose every feature the stem pre-excludes is not a competitor.

Cueing (lexical match): the stem's ECG line hands the candidate 'ST depression' - i.e. explicitly not ST elevation - and the key is worded 'Non-ST-elevation acute coronary syndrome'. A candidate with no cardiology can match the negative in the stem to the negative in the option label.

Cueing (format outlier): option D is the longest option (5 words) against 'Acute aortic dissection' (3), 'Pulmonary embolism' (2) and 'Acute pericarditis' (2), and is the only option that names a syndrome category rather than a single discrete disease entity.

Minor rationale inaccuracy (not scored fatal): the key rationale says 'The three alternatives each have a defining feature that the stem reports and finds absent:' and then lists six features including 'there is no reflux symptom'. Reflux/GERD is not one of the three alternatives; claim CLM-GERD-01 is admitted with no corresponding option, so the stem line 'he has no heartburn or regurgitation' rules out an option that was never offered.

Cueing (hedge word): the key is the only option carrying a hedge - 'Give a cautious intravenous fluid bolus and reassess fluid responsiveness'. 'Cautious' plus a built-in reassessment step is the classic test-wiseness signature of the safe/correct option; the three distractors are all unhedged commitments ('Give intravenous metoprolol...', 'Give intravenous furosemide...', 'Give sublingual nitroglycerin...').

Cueing (grammatical/format outlier): the three distractors share an identical frame of action-plus-justification - 'to reduce myocardial oxygen demand', 'for the raised jugular venous pressure', 'for the ischaemic pain' - while the key alone replaces the justification tail with a second action, 'and reassess fluid responsiveness'. Three parallel options and one structurally different option makes the different one recognisable without the medicine.
Cueing (only one of its type): the key is the only non-pharmacological option; A, C and D each name a specific drug (metoprolol, furosemide, nitroglycerin).

Medicine, numbers and evidence all check out: 'ST elevation in leads II, III and aVF' with 'ST elevation in V4R', BP 84/56 mmHg, HR 58 beats/min, raised JVP with clear lungs is right-ventricular infarction physiology, and claim CLM-ACS-RV-INFARCTION-STABILIZATION-01 directly supports preload optimisation and the avoidance of nitrates, diuretics and beta blockade. Distractors A, C and D each have a genuine positive stem anchor ('crushing chest pain', 'jugular venous pressure is elevated to the angle of the jaw', 'an hour of crushing chest pain' respectively).

Metadata inconsistency (not scored): declared item_archetype is 'RISK_STRATIFICATION', but the lead-in is 'What is the most appropriate next step in his management?' and the options are four therapies. The item selects a treatment; it does not stratify risk. Also, admitted claim CLM-ACS-AMI-CARDIOGENIC-SHOCK-01 is load-bearing for no option, since 'the catheterisation laboratory has been activated' is already given in the stem.

Numbers verified: 'about four hours' first-medical-contact-to-device exceeds the 120-minute threshold in claim CLM-ACS-PHARMACOINVASIVE-01, and '40 minutes after the sudden onset' makes her the 'early low-bleeding-risk presenter' the same claim describes as suited to a pharmacoinvasive strategy. Option A's 'three to five days' correctly falls outside the claim's 'angiography within 24 hours'. The decisive 120-minute threshold is deliberately not written into the stem, so the candidate must supply it.

The stem does not name the threshold or the strategy, so the item cannot be answered lexically. All four options are the same kind of thing (reperfusion strategies) at the same grain, and none stands out by length (13-15 words each) or grammar (all verb-initial).

Each distractor has a positive stem anchor: A and D are invited by 'a remote northern community' reached only 'by fixed-wing air transfer' plus 'She is alert and comfortable at rest'; C is invited by 'The nearest hospital with a catheterisation laboratory' and the absence of any contraindication ('has never had a stroke or intracranial bleeding, has had no recent surgery, trauma or bleeding, takes no anticoagulant').

The distinction tested is genuinely two-step - lysis versus primary PCI, then what follows lysis - so it is not answerable by recalling a single fact, and it is pitched at entry-to-supervised-practice level.

Key and rationales are entailed by claim CLM-ACS-NSTE-HIGH-RISK-DISPOSITION-01, which states the high-risk criteria hold 'even if symptoms resolve' and that 'discharge, outpatient stress testing, or observation without an invasive plan are reserved for lower-risk or diagnostically uncertain presentations'. No rationale asserts anything beyond the admitted evidence.

Distractor anchors are real and written in the stem: B is anchored by 'She feels well and wants to go home to her grandchildren' and 'the current tracing has returned to her baseline'; A and D are anchored by 'Her examination is normal' and the complete resolution of the episode. The temptation is exactly the reasoning trap the item declares.
Options are balanced (9-11 words), all verb-initial, all disposition decisions at the same grain, so no option is identifiable by format.

Noted but not scored as a defect: 'Serial high-sensitivity troponin values show a rise and then a fall' in a patient presenting 'six hours after' the episode is on the early side for a demonstrated fall, but the stem does not state the sampling times and the admitted claim's criterion is 'a rise or fall in troponin compatible with MI', so nothing candidate-facing is wrong.

Reasoning demand is on the lower side - the item is close to a single-rule application - but it does require the candidate to resist symptom and ECG resolution as a reason to de-escalate, which is a defensible entry-to-practice judgement rather than buzzword matching.

COMPETITOR_WITHOUT_STEM_ANCHOR (option C, Foreign body aspiration): the stem supplies no feature that would draw a candidate toward it and instead pre-excludes it twice over - 'There was no choking episode and nothing was seen in his mouth' and 'air entry is equal throughout, with no focal area of reduced or altered air entry'. There is no sudden onset, no asymmetry, no focal finding. A candidate need not know any paediatrics to strike it out.

COMPETITOR_WITHOUT_STEM_ANCHOR (option B, First presentation of asthma): every feature that would make asthma live is written as absent - 'This is the first time he has ever wheezed', 'has no eczema or other atopy and there is no family history of asthma' - and the wheeze is explicitly preceded by a viral prodrome. The distractor rationale concedes the option needs 'an older infant or child with recurrent episodes or atopy, or with wheeze that is not preceded by a viral upper respiratory prodrome', none of which the stem provides.

Cueing (the stem pre-answers the question): 'his illness has followed the course his parents were told to expect' tells the candidate that a prior working diagnosis is holding and that no alternative needs to be considered, in an item whose lead-in is 'What is the most likely diagnosis?'. The same clause is then used to knock out option D ('the illness is following the expected course'). A stem that certifies its own diagnosis undercuts a diagnostic lead-in.

Cueing (definitional restatement): the stem reproduces the elements of admitted claim CLM-R2-PED-DX-ANCHOR nearly item-by-item - 'the third day of an illness that began with fever, cough and a runny nose', 'the first time he has ever wheezed', age 7 months, 'widespread symmetric expiratory wheeze with fine crackles' - so the item is answerable by matching a memorised definition rather than by discriminating between the offered diagnoses.

Medicine and numbers are correct: RR 52 is tachypnoeic for a 7-month-old, temperature 38.1 degrees Celsius and saturation 94% in room air are internally consistent with mild-to-moderate bronchiolitis, and 94% correctly sits above the 90% oxygen threshold used elsewhere in this set. Option D (pneumonia) does retain a genuine positive anchor in 'temperature is 38.1 degrees Celsius' and 'fine crackles in both lung fields'.

UNSUPPORTED_CLAIM (distractor C rationale): 'A complete blood count has not been found useful for predicting serious bacterial infection in this illness' is asserted as fact, but this item's admitted evidence is only CLM-R4-PED-MONITORING, CLM-R4-PED-CONTINUOUS and CLM-R2-PED-INV-ANCHOR. None of the three says anything about the complete blood count or about predicting serious bacterial infection; CLM-R2-PED-INV-ANCHOR says only that 'Diagnostic studies are not indicated for most children with bronchiolitis'. The load-bearing sentence for eliminating C rests on nothing admitted.

UNSUPPORTED_CLAIM (distractor D rationale): 'A radiograph is considered when the diagnosis is unclear, when the rate of improvement is not as expected, or when severity raises other diagnostic possibilities such as bacterial pneumonia.' This is CLM-R2-PED-CXR-INDICATION, which is admitted to G2-PED-01, not to this item. Within G2-PED-02's own admitted evidence the entire criterion used to reject option D is absent.

UNSUPPORTED_CLAIM (distractor D rationale, second sentence): 'Radiographs in this illness often show non-specific patchy change that invites treatment the infant does not need' is not stated by any admitted claim in this item.

COMPETITOR_WITHOUT_STEM_ANCHOR (option C, Complete blood count and blood culture): nothing in the stem invites a septic workup. There is no fever, no deterioration, no feeding failure and no diagnostic doubt - the stem states 'The diagnosis has not been in doubt at any point and her course has been as expected' and describes an infant who 'has been weaned off supplemental oxygen this morning' and 'is breastfeeding to her usual volume'. The rationale tries to supply the missing anchor from outside the stem: 'Sending blood is the reflex response to an admitted febrile infant' - but this infant is never described as febrile.

COMPETITOR_WITHOUT_STEM_ANCHOR (option D, Chest radiograph): the stem again supplies no trigger and instead explicitly negates all three triggers the rationale names, in one sentence: 'The diagnosis has not been in doubt at any point and her course has been as expected.'

Decision granularity: options A and B are continuing monitoring strategies spanning the admission, while C and D are one-off diagnostic tests. 'Regular structured clinical assessment with intermittent oxygen saturation measurement' is a plan of care; 'Chest radiograph' is a single investigation ordered once. These are not the same grain of decision. The declared option_set_archetype 'INVESTIGATION_SET' compounds this, since the key is not an investigation at all.

Cueing (length and type): the key is 9 words - 'Regular structured clinical assessment with intermittent oxygen saturation measurement' - against 6, 6 and 2 words for the distractors, with 'Chest radiograph' conspicuously short. The key is also the only option that is a repeated clinical process rather than a machine or a test, in a set whose lead-in asks which 'assessment' is appropriate.

Cueing (meta-clauses that clear the field): 'She is in a single room and no cohorting decision is outstanding' and 'The diagnosis has not been in doubt at any point' are not clinical findings; they are instructions to the candidate about which options are off the table.

The keyed answer itself is correct and well supported by CLM-R4-PED-MONITORING and CLM-R4-PED-CONTINUOUS, which name exactly this patient - 'feeding well, weaning from supplemental oxygen and showing improvement in work of breathing' - as the one for whom intermittent monitoring is appropriate; option A is the only distractor with a real stem anchor ('weaned off supplemental oxygen this morning').

Cueing (grammatical outlier): the key is the only option written as an imperative clause - 'Begin low-flow supplemental oxygen by nasal prongs' - while all three distractors are bare noun phrases: 'High-flow nasal cannula oxygen', 'Nebulized epinephrine', 'Nasogastric maintenance fluids'. It is also the longest option (7 words against 4, 2 and 3). A test-wise candidate can identify the key on grammar alone.

Cueing (meta-clause removing a distractor): 'no member of the team has raised the question of non-invasive support or intensive care' is not a clinical finding about the patient; it is a statement about what the team has said, and its only function is to tell the candidate not to pick option A. The distractor rationale confirms this use: 'non-invasive support is not under consideration'.

Numbers verified and correctly applied: 'oxygen saturation of 88% in room air on two separate measurements twenty minutes apart' sits below the threshold in CLM-R2-PED-OXYGEN ('Oxygen should be administered if saturations fall below 90% and used to maintain saturations at or above 90%'), the 90% figure is not disclosed in the stem, and RR 58 is tachypnoeic but not itself a feeding contraindication for a 5-month-old.

Distractors are genuinely anchored: A by 'moderate subcostal recession' and the hypoxaemia itself, C by 'taking about two thirds of her usual feeds' and 'a respiratory rate of 58 breaths/min', B by the respiratory distress. All four options are next actions at the same grain, and the rejections of A, B and C are each entailed by CLM-R4-PED-HFNC and CLM-R4-PED-EPINEPHRINE respectively or by the stem's feeding description.

Admitted claims CLM-R2-PED-SALBUTAMOL and CLM-R4-PED-HYPERTONIC are load-bearing for no option in this item (no bronchodilator or hypertonic saline option is offered); this is surplus evidence rather than a defect in the item.
